plan.intent: Put ONE attempt-resolution rule in the fleet, in the module the other readers already import, and route verify-state.py own two verdict reads through it. Add to verify-state.py: review_attempts(review) -> ordered list, treating the top-level {verdict, attempt, summary, findings} as attempt 1 and walking attempt_2, attempt_3, ... stopping at the FIRST GAP; final_verdict(review) -> the LAST attempt; ever_rejected(review) -> True when ANY attempt is REJECT; plus a slice-level convenience over state+sid. This mirrors fleetview/index.html:628-644 deliberately and by reference (read-only, not touched, not imported). CAP DECISION: match fleetview bound exactly - the walk stops after attempt_9, because fleetview loop is `for (i = 2; i < 10; i++)` and two readers with different caps is precisely the divergence this slice exists to prevent. But do NOT match it silently: if attempt_10 or beyond is present, the helper reports it loudly (a finding the audit surfaces), because at that point the board and the fleet WOULD disagree and a human must know rather than be quietly given one of two answers. resolve() itself stays a dumb dotted-path walker and is NOT made attempt-aware - a magic resolve would silently change every unrelated dotted read in three scripts. Then rewire verify-state.py two sites: line 261 (the status-done audit line) and line 283 (the integrator fan-in check). FAN-IN RULE, reasoned not asserted: the check today means 'a fan-in happened over a slice that never passed'. A state.json carries no ordering between the integrator write and a re-review write, so 'merged before the re-review landed' is not detectable from this file by any rule and never was. The two available rules are (a) latest attempt is not PASS, and (b) ever_rejected. (b) would fire on EVERY run that ever looped - the normal, intended workflow - and would repeat the 2026-08-26 failure recorded at verify-state.py:220 where the check fired on every run reaching an integrator and no diamond could close. So (a): the check meaning legitimately narrows to 'no slice is CURRENTLY REJECT at fan-in', a slice whose latest attempt is REJECT still blocks fan-in, and ever_rejected is display-only and must never become a blocker anywhere.

architect.rationale:
SHAPE IS FORCED, not chosen - recorded as such. feature-graph step 0.5 check 2: this run edits graph_agents/.claude/agents/reviewer.md and integrator.md and the close-run skill, the definitions the fleet spawns from, and agent registration happens at session start. A fan-out here would spawn builders from the definitions being rewritten mid-run. graph_agents IS a git repo (branching and rollback exist), so the forcing reason is spawn-definition editing alone, not absence of isolation. Slice count does not enter into it.

ON THE SCOUT PLAN-KILLER, and I agree with it: the deliverable is ONE shared helper with every caller routed through it, not three independent edits. verify.resolve() is a dumb dotted-path walker and, worse, is not really shared - brief.py reads through its own Reader.get() and has a degraded fallback that is a second implementation waiting to happen. Four readers with four rules is how this defect comes back. So s1 puts the rule in verify-state.py, the module close-run.py and brief.py ALREADY import via importlib, and s2/s3 route through it rather than restating it. Two design decisions inside that: resolve() itself is NOT made attempt-aware (a magic resolve silently changes every unrelated dotted read in three scripts); and brief.py degraded fallback does not reimplement the rule, it says it is degraded.

ON FLEETVIEW: read-only, out of scope, not touched, not imported - separate repo, and importing it would be the cross-app edge the umbrella invariant forbids. index.html:628-644 is the REFERENCE the fleet copies by reading, which is exactly copy-dont-couple. CAP DECISION, made deliberately: the fleet helper MATCHES fleetview bound - the walk stops after attempt_9, because fleetview loop is for (i = 2; i < 10; i++) and two readers with different caps recreates the divergence in a place nobody would look. Where they would silently differ, at attempt_10 and beyond, the fleet helper is LOUD rather than quietly authoritative. Both readers keep the stop-at-first-gap rule.

ON THE FAN-IN CHECK at verify-state.py:283, reasoned rather than asserted: its meaning DOES change, and narrowing it is correct. A state.json has no ordering between the integrator write and a re-review write, so 'merged before the re-review landed' was never detectable from this file. The alternative rule - block fan-in when any attempt ever REJECTed - would fire on every run that looped, which is the intended workflow, and would repeat the 2026-08-26 breakage recorded in verify-state.py:220 where no diamond could close. So the check becomes 'no slice LATEST attempt is REJECT'. A slice still sitting at REJECT continues to block fan-in and continues to block a close. ever_rejected is display-only, forever; if it ever becomes a blocker the fleet stops being able to loop.

ON THE REGRESSION THIS RUN EXISTS NOT TO CAUSE - a fix that launders rejections. It is defended in three places on purpose, because one place is a single point of failure: s1 ships ever_rejected and a test that a re-review REJECT is final; s2 ships case (c), top PASS + attempt_2 REJECT still blocks the close, which is the one case a 'did any attempt pass' implementation fails; s3 requires the board row for a REJECT-then-PASS slice to be non-identical to a first-try PASS. Blast radius is verified, never targeted: fleet-hardening audit must go from 4 violations to exactly 2, and BOTH survivors - closing_fix has no review, and no authorship stamps - are asserted present in s1 and s2 done_when, so a fix that makes fleet-hardening closeable fails the gate.

SCOUT UNKNOWNS, both closed by the orchestrator recorded scope decision and folded in here: #2, attempts survive permanently and the latest supplies the verdict - no flattening, no migration, and no existing run state.json is edited (those are reviewers keys and rewriting one would forge the authorship written_by exists to catch). #1, brief.py tries count IS folded in - it reads the resolved attempt list, not the top-level field, so the board stops saying 'attempt 1' over a hidden attempt_2.

RISK TAGS: four high, one low, and the low is the deliberate one. s4 (_schema.json) is low not because it is small - it is the highest-leverage file in the run - but because its one real failure mode, a template key that changes placeholder identity, is fully visible to its done_when in both directions (before/after audit diff over all 10 runs on disk, plus a fresh-template fixture and a real-re-review fixture). The four high slices are high for reasons a green test cannot cover: s1 is imported by everything and carries the anti-laundering primitive; s2 certifies runs as done and has one failure mode only a single case catches; s3 real property is 'a human reads this row as a loop'; s5 is prose in the files the fleet spawns from, where grep proves presence and nothing proves clarity.

not_doing: NOT flattening attempt_N or migrating attempts to the top level. The nested shape is correct and stays - two reviewers invented it independently and fleetview already reads it.

NOT editing any existing run state.json - not payload-split, not fleetview-payload, not fleet-hardening. Those are reviewers keys; relocating a verdict would leave a key stamped written_by:reviewer with someone else as its real author, which is the forgery written_by exists to catch.

NOT adding timestamps or write-ordering to state.json to distinguish 'merged before the re-review landed'. That information was never in the file and inventing a way to carry it is a different run.
NOT touching builders.<slice>.attempt (brief.py:271-273) - the build try count is a different field with a different meaning.
NOT adding a registry entry for graph_agents, noted in passing by the orchestrator pre-flight. Separate task.
